reasons.plausibility: Substituting Hf with Al in a BCC refractory high-entropy alloy is highly likely to form brittle intermetallics (e.g., B2, Laves phases) rather than a single-phase BCC solid solution, severely degrading ductility and high-temperature strength, contradicting well-established phase formation rules.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and well-defined, with specific compositions, processing, test conditions, and quantitative falsification criteria (≥10% density reduction, ≥90% strength retention) that would decisively prove the hypothesis wrong.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it proposes an intervention (Al substitution) that is fundamentally unsound for this alloy class, and testing it would waste resources on a predictable failure.
